chemical-heat-water-1ced12d9ab9a80752fd2.name: market for heat, from steam, in chemical industry, composed from resolved suppliers, RER
chemical-heat-water-1ced12d9ab9a80752fd2.rationale: Reviewed chemical-plant heat service per MJ, with retained source make-up water and physical water releases. The native original XML explicitly defines one MJ of heat for chemical-process steam and excludes its water input because steam is often used in closed systems. Use that complete positive-reference MJ heat service once, then retain every inspected source tap-water coefficient and both direct water releases separately. Do not use the kg-based fresh-steam process, the old rounded 0.36 kg/MJ factor, or 1 MJ per kg. The two exact markets have only one local unit share of the inspected energy producer; flatten that unit share without adding a second heat service. The target approximates the source regional fuel and electricity mix, combustion efficiencies, technology, vintage, allocation and infrastructure; their LCIA equivalence is not established. Water uses complete native water supply as a geography/vintage proxy, preserving each source provider share separately without normalization. Do not add the original source fuel/electricity inputs to the complete native heat service or count water twice. Canonical water identity, receiving compartment, unit and signed amount remain exact; unsupported native physical water definitions must remain unresolved, never omitted. Factor +1 preserves caller signed MJ, supported uncertainty, formulas, metadata, foreground suppliers and separately listed emissions. Internal source uncertainty/formulas are not reconstructed. Only the 36 enumerated cut-off source profiles are reviewed. Physical kg-steam, allocated chemical co-product steam, individual steam transport, consequential inventories and missing profiles cannot inherit this review. The reverse native heat service has a different water boundary and remains unsupported until separately reviewed; no inverse or water cancellation is inferred.

fuels-38-chemical-heat-uq-b79ce56ce460b4.name: Chemical-steam heat, source 3.8 RoW water quantities and uncertainty retained
fuels-38-chemical-heat-uq-b79ce56ce460b4.rationale: Exact inspected ecoinvent 3.8 cut-off RoW chemical-steam heat market only. Both source references are positive one MJ of thermal energy, not kg fresh steam. Flatten only its original unit supplier share. The original native XML defines one MJ chemical-process heat and excludes water for closed steam systems. Retain that complete native positive-MJ heat service once, all seven separate source make-up-water shares and both physical water releases. This scoped refinement preserves original lognormal amount/loc/scale, pedigree and supported statistics on all nine retained water exchanges; no renormalization, omission or water-density/steam-mass factor is added. Use complete native Swiss tap water as the existing geographic/vintage screening proxy, with original source-provider quantities and uncertainty retained separately. Keep exact canonical water name, compartment, m3 and sign. Do not add source fuel/electricity inputs to complete native heat, use the old rounded 0.36 kg/MJ factor, or duplicate water supply. Two original background water-release formulas reference the original producer parameter context; they are not published or transplanted into the native helper. Preserve caller formulas and uncertainty; background parameterization/correlations and source energy-system uncertainty are not reconstructed. The inherited global review describes older helpers; this exact 3.8 recipe additionally retains water marginal uncertainty. Native regional fuel/electricity mixes, combustion efficiency, technology, infrastructure, allocation, geography, vintage and internal uncertainty differ, with unquantified score effects. Physical kg-steam, co-product steam and other uninspected profiles cannot inherit this correspondence.
